title: Affine higher-direct-image support bound at adic field coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine finite-type $k$-morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the adic category $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], its standard constructible heart $\operatorname{Sh}_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], and the derived direct image $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $F\in\operatorname{Sh}_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ and let $a\ge0$ be an integer with $\dim\operatorname{Supp}F\le a$. Here $\operatorname{Supp}$ denotes the Zariski closure of the nonzero-geometric-fibre locus, and dimension and the empty-support convention are those of [def-per-support-condition]. Then for every $q\ge0$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)\le a-q.$$
Also $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)=0$ for $q<0$. All cohomology objects are those of the standard t-structure of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres].

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1, the sheaf estimate d(R^i f_*F) <= d(F)-i; finite-coefficient calculation: Stacks Tag 0F0X, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-interlude-I; adic interpretation: Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: The schemes $X,Y$ are noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is noetherian, and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], choose a finite coefficient field $E$ and $F_E\in\operatorname{Sh}_c(X,E)$ representing $F$. The same node computes fibres at the common stage by extension from $E$ to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. A vector space is zero if and only if its extension to a field is zero (a basis remains linearly independent). Thus $F_E$ has the same nonzero-fibre locus and the same closed support $Z$ as $F$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, choose its uniformizer $\varpi$, and write $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$. The heart assertion of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] supplies an integral heart object $H$ with $Q_XH\cong F_E$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Proposition 6.8.11(3); finite-stage and heart reductions

proof.text: Give $Z$ its reduced induced closed scheme structure $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the complementary open. It is quasi-compact since $X$ is noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], the restricted coefficient rings are $B_Z,E_Z$ and $B_U,E_U$. Form the actual module sheaf $K=i_*i^{-1}H$. The ringed open-closed lemma makes $i_*$ exact and gives $j^{-1}K=0$ and $i^{-1}i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$. Restrict a finite stratification for $H$ to $Z$, and add the zero stratum $U$: on each resulting piece $K$ is locally a completed coefficient module associated to a finitely presented $A$-module, or zero. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] puts $K[0]$ in the integral constructible category, including compatible etale-origin witnesses. This construction permits torsion in $H$ and in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); closed-support restriction and extension

proof.text: Write $J_T$ for [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. Its t-exact realization and restriction comparison identify $J_X(F_E)$ with $E_X\otimes_{B_X}H$ and its restriction to $U$ with $J_U(j^*F_E)$. The latter is zero: all its adic fibres vanish by the definition of $Z$, and [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] makes those fibres conservative. The open-closed short exact sequence consequently gives $J_X(F_E)\cong i_*i^{-1}J_X(F_E)$. Localization is the sheaf colimit of repeated multiplication by $\varpi$. It commutes with $i^{-1}$, and with $i_*$ by the filtered-colimit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], since $X$ is qcqs. The coefficient restriction isomorphisms from Step 2 therefore identify $J_X(Q_XK)=E_X\otimes_{B_X}K$ with $i_*i^{-1}J_X(F_E)$. Full faithfulness of $J_X$ gives $Q_XK\cong F_E$. We have obtained an integral heart representative supported on $Z$, without assuming that an arbitrary original representative $H$ has that support.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; supported integral representative

proof.text: Let $K_1=K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/\varpi)_X$. The two-term resolution of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] identifies it, after restriction of scalars, with $\operatorname{Cone}(\varpi:K\to K)$. Thus its only possible cohomology sheaves are $K[\varpi]$ in degree $-1$ and $K/\varpi K$ in degree zero, by the kernel/cokernel clause of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Choose an etale-origin witness $L_1\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A/\varpi)$ for $K_1$, as supplied by membership in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. The comparison inverse image is exact by [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and fully faithful by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. It follows that $L_1$ has only $T=\mathcal H^{-1}L_1$ and $G=\mathcal H^0L_1$, and both are supported on $Z$: restriction of $K_1$ to $U$ is zero, and comparison on $U$ is faithful. They are sheaves of modules over the finite ring $A/\varpi$, hence are torsion abelian sheaves after forgetting scalars.

source.place: Definitions 6.5.1 and 6.8.10; the uniformizer cone; Lemma 5.4.3

proof.text: For any $x\in Z$, its irreducible closed closure $C=\overline{\{x\}}$ lies in $Z$. The dimension formula [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)=\dim C\le\dim Z\le a$. The middle inequality follows directly by viewing each irreducible closed chain in $C$ as one in $Z$. Thus the supports of the underlying abelian sheaves of $T,G$ lie in $E_a(X)$, in the notation of [lem-kun-affine-direct-image-support-bound]. Apply that node to both sheaves: $\operatorname{supp}R^rf_*T\subset E_{a-r}(Y)$ and $\operatorname{supp}R^rf_*G\subset E_{a-r}(Y)$ for $r\ge0$. Its hypotheses hold because $f$ is affine over $k$, $X,Y$ are finite type over $k$, and both input sheaves are torsion. The module/abelian comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies these bounds with the bounds for module-valued higher direct images.

The ordinary truncation triangle is $T[1]\to L_1\to G\to T[2]$. Apply the triangulated derived direct image of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] and take the long exact cohomology sequence, as in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. For $q\ge0$ it contains $R^{q+1}f_*T\to\mathcal H^q(Rf_*L_1)\to R^qf_*G$. Step 5 bounds the outer supports by $E_{a-q-1}(Y)$ and $E_{a-q}(Y)$, respectively. Since the first set is contained in the second, exactness of etale geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $\operatorname{supp}\mathcal H^q(Rf_*L_1)\subset E_{a-q}(Y)$. This explicitly includes the degree $-1$ Tor term of the derived reduction. It does not replace $K_1$ by the ordinary quotient $K/\varpi K$.

source.place: Tag 0F0X applied to the two cohomology sheaves; ordinary truncation triangle and its long exact sequence

proof.text:
Put $M=Rf_*K$ integrally. The theorem [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible], applied over the field $k$ with $\ell$ invertible, makes $M$ bounded constructible and gives $M\otimes^L(A/\varpi)\cong Rf_{*,1}K_1$. Under [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], the right side is $
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_1$. Here $f$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Each $N_q=\mathcal H^q(M)$ is an integral heart object by [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]. The uniformizer cone from [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] and the long exact sequence from [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] give a monomorphism $N_q/\varpi N_q\hookrightarrow\mathcal H^q(M\otimes^L(A/\varpi))$. By [lem-a1-integral-constructible-reduction-fibres] its source is $
u_Y^*C_q$ for a constructible etale sheaf $C_q$. The target is $
u_Y^*\mathcal H^q(Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_1)$. Exact full faithfulness of comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] reflects this monomorphism and supplies the etale monomorphism $C_q\hookrightarrow\mathcal H^q(Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_1)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 and its reduction comparison; Lemma 5.4.3; Proposition 6.8.11(3)

proof.text: Fix $q\ge0$ and a geometric point $\bar y$ over $y\notin E_{a-q}(Y)$. Steps 6--7 and exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] give $(C_q)_{\bar y}=0$. By [lem-a1-integral-constructible-reduction-fibres], the adic integral fibre module $P_{\bar y}$ of $N_q$ is finite over $A$ and $P_{\bar y}/\varpi P_{\bar y}\cong(C_q)_{\bar y}=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with the local ring $A$, maximal ideal $(\varpi)$, and submodule zero, to get $P_{\bar y}=0$. Its rational fibre $P_{\bar y}\otimes_AE$ is therefore zero. The cohomology comparison in [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] gives $Q_YN_q\cong\mathcal H^q(Q_YM)$. By [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] and Step 3, $Q_YM\cong Rf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}F_E$. Thus the nonzero-fibre locus of $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}F_E)$ is contained in $E_{a-q}(Y)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), Proposition 6.8.14(2); Nakayama: Stacks Tag 00DV, algebra-lemma-NAK (4)

proof.text: Finite coefficient extension commutes with direct image by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and with standard cohomology and geometric fibres by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. Passing to the common finite-stage category therefore identifies the output in Step 8 with $\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)$ after extending fibres to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Faithful extension of vector spaces preserves their zero locus. This output is constructible: integral direct-image constructibility in Step 7 and rational transport put it in the constructible category, and its cohomology is in the constructible heart. Its nonzero-fibre locus $S$ is consequently constructible by [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]. We have proved $S\subset E_{a-q}(Y)$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2) and Remark 6.8.15; common finite coefficient stages

proof.text: Set $b=a-q$. If $b<0$, then $E_b(Y)=\varnothing$, so Step 9 gives $S=\varnothing$ and the claimed empty-support bound. Suppose $b\ge0$. For each irreducible component $C$ of $\overline S$, its generic point $\eta_C$ belongs to $S$. Indeed, write the constructible set $S$ as a finite union of locally closed subsets and then their irreducible pieces; the closure of at least one piece is $C$, and that piece contains an open dense subset of $C$, hence its generic point. Now [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\eta_C)\le b$. Every irreducible closed chain in the finite union $\overline S=\bigcup C$ lies in a component, so $\dim\overline S\le b$. Since $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^q(Rf_*F)=\overline S$ by the given closed-support convention, this proves the stated inequality. Constructibility is essential here; no dimension bound for the closure of an arbitrary subset of $E_b(Y)$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0B1C, item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg of lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic; finite constructible decomposition

proof.text: For the negative-degree assertion put $R=Rf_*F$. The ordinary adjunction [lem-per-qbar-ordinary-adjunction] applies to $f$, since it is affine, hence separated, and finite type. Let $A_-=\tau^{\le-1}R$ in the bounded standard t-structure. By [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], it is built by finitely many truncation triangles from the objects $\mathcal H^j(A_-)[-j]$ with $j\le-1$. The pullback of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] is triangulated and carries each heart object into the heart. Extension closure therefore gives $Lf^*A_-\in D^{\le-1}(X)$. Orthogonality of the standard t-structure gives $\operatorname{Hom}(Lf^*A_-,F)=0$, so adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A_-,R)=0$. In particular the canonical truncation map $A_-\to R$ is zero. In each degree $j<0$ it induces the canonical isomorphism on cohomology. A zero morphism which is an isomorphism has zero source and target, so $\mathcal H^j(R)=0$ for every $j<0$.
